chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is befitting for the sick person among you to inform his brothers of his illness, so they visit him, and he is rewarded through them, and they are rewarded through him.'
He said: So it was said to him: 'Yes, they are rewarded for their walking to him, so how is he rewarded through them?'

He (the narrator) said: So he (the Imam) said: 'By earning good deeds for them, he is rewarded through them. Ten good deeds are written for him for that, ten ranks are raised for him, and ten evil deeds are erased from him.'

key_terms.الدَّرَجَاتُ: Degrees/ranks — elevated spiritual stations in the afterlife
key_terms.السَّيِّئَاتُ: Evil deeds/sins — recorded transgressions that are here erased as a reward
key_terms.الْحَسَنَاتِ: Good deeds/merits — acts that earn spiritual reward, recorded in one's account
key_terms.يَعُودُونَهُ: They visit the sick (عيادة) — visiting the sick is a highly recommended act in Islamic tradition
key_terms.يَنْبَغِي: It is befitting/proper — a term indicating strong recommendation (mustahabb) rather than strict obligation
key_terms.يُؤْذِنَ: To inform/permit — here meaning to make one's illness known so others may come to visit

ai.seo_question: What reward does a sick Muslim earn for informing others of his illness so they can visit him?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that it is commendable for a sick believer to inform his fellow believers of his illness, enabling them to perform the act of visiting the sick (ziyarat al-marid), which is a recommended communal duty in Islam. The teaching addresses a profound theological point: not only do the visitors earn spiritual reward for their effort in walking to visit the sick, but the sick person himself earns reward by making his illness known and thereby enabling others to perform this good deed. The Imam quantifies the reward: ten good deeds recorded, ten ranks elevated, and ten sins expunged — underscoring the immense spiritual value of this mutual act of care within the believing community.
